name: bolognese
instructions:
TWO BOLOGNESE VARIANTS. Both share: tomato base + a protein + wine (white and/or red — both appear frequently across canonical bolognese recipes) + soffrito-style aromatics + long simmer intent + pasta. Variant A is the canonical bolognese and gets the headline treatment; variant B is the vegetarian/vegan reinterpretation that follows the bolognese SHAPE without trying to be Marcella's dish.

MUSHROOMS ARE OUT: earlier this file included two mushroom-based variants (ATK mushroom bolognese and my mushroom+lentil mix). Both removed. Lentils and toasted walnuts are the vegetarian protein path; mushrooms distract with the onion/celery/carrot base and start to read stew rather than bolognese. If you want a mushroom-forward pasta, see [[pasta-al-funghi]] (lean) or [[boscaiola]] (rich) instead.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA BOLOGNESE (CANONICAL) ===

The load-bearing recipe in this family. Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking. If 'bolognese' means one thing in this cookbook, it's this one.

INGREDIENTS:
- vegetable oil + butter (the fat)
- yellow onions, celery, carrots — finely diced soffrito
- ground beef (or impossible meat as the substitute)
- milk
- nutmeg
- WHITE wine (Marcella's canonical; red wine also appears in some bolognese traditions — see WINE note)
- canned tomatoes
- black pepper
- pasta (traditionally tagliatelle, not spaghetti)
- parmesan cheese for serving

TECHNIQUE — MARCELLA'S NON-NEGOTIABLES:
1. Cook the beef ONLY until it loses raw color. Do NOT brown it. Browning gives a different (and lesser) ragu.
2. Milk goes in BEFORE wine. The milk coats the meat and protects it from the wine acid; reversing the order changes the texture.
3. Bare-simmer for THREE+ HOURS uncovered. Splash in water if it dries out. The long uncovered simmer is what makes it a bolognese; cutting time turns it into a generic meat sauce.
4. Fat should separate at the end. That's the visual signal you're done.

=== VARIANT B — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE (VEGAN, TOMATO-PASTE-FORWARD) ===

From Nisha Vora / Rainbow Plant Life. Follows a traditionally-bolognese technique (tomato paste caramelized in the fond, red wine deglaze, long simmer, balsamic finish). Red lentils + finely chopped TOASTED WALNUTS do the meat-analog work; the tomato paste + crushed tomatoes carry the umami. ~55 min total, much faster than the 3-hour bolognese in variant A. NO MUSHROOMS — lentils + toasted walnuts are the vegetarian protein path here.

INGREDIENTS (serves 6):
- 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or more oregano if you don't have thyme)
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- freshly ground black pepper
- 1 (5.3-oz / 150g) TUBE of tomato paste (see notes — tube is load-bearing, not canned)
- 1/2 cup (120mL) dry RED wine (recommended — malbec / chianti / tempranillo / sangiovese / merlot / cabernet sauvignon / pinot noir / syrah). Nisha's canonical; white wine also works if that's what you have — see WINE note.
- 3 cups (720mL) vegetable broth
- 1 cup (185g) RED lentils, soaked 30-60 min first (see notes)
- 1/4 cup (32g) TOASTED walnuts, crushed finely (see notes)
- 1 (14.5-oz / 410g) can crushed tomatoes OR whole peeled tomatoes crushed by hand
- 12-16 oz pasta (long-wide preferred: tagliatelle, pappardelle, fettuccine; ridged tube also works: rigatoni, penne rigate; gnocchi works)
- 1 tbsp high-quality aged balsamic vinegar (or 1-2 tsp brown/coconut/cane sugar as a sub)
- flat-leaf parsley, chopped, for garnish

PROCEDURE:
1. Soak the red lentils in cool water for 30-60 min. Meanwhile, prep everything else (chop onion + garlic, TOAST + finely chop walnuts).
2. Heat 12-inch deep sauté pan or Dutch oven on medium-high. Add olive oil; when shimmering, add onions + pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until light-brown fond forms on the pan surface (~5 min). Deglaze with a few spoons of water and stir. Continue cooking, adding more water every few minutes and stirring frequently to prevent burning, until onions are softened and golden brown (9-10 min total).
3. Add garlic, thyme, oregano, 1 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper. Stir frequently, cook 60-90 sec.
4. Stir in the ENTIRE TUBE OF TOMATO PASTE. Cook 2-3 min, stirring very frequently, until it caramelizes and turns darker red.
5. DEGLAZE WITH RED WINE (recommended): pour in wine, scrape up browned bits, cook 1-2 min until alcohol smell burns off and mixture is jammy.
6. Pour in vegetable broth to deglaze. Add drained lentils and crushed TOASTED walnuts; stir. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low for a rapid simmer, cook 20 min stirring occasionally.
7. Add the crushed tomatoes. Simmer another 15-20 min (or 20 min for more developed flavor) until lentils are tender but still al dente. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. If using crushed tomatoes (not whole crushed by hand), may need a little water or lower heat.
8. Meanwhile, cook pasta in generously salted water to just al dente. Reserve a ladle of pasta water. Drain (don't rinse).
9. Taste for seasoning. Finish the bolognese with the balsamic vinegar (or sugar sub) and stir.
10. Add the hot pasta to the bolognese, toss until coated, add pasta water as needed. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes:
THE BOLOGNESE SHAPE — WHAT BOTH VARIANTS HAVE IN COMMON:
1. A tomato base (canned tomatoes + often tomato paste; regular canned only — no fire-roasted; that's fire-roasted-meatballs.json).
2. A protein slot: real meat (A) OR lentils + toasted walnuts (B). MUSHROOMS ARE OUT (see MUSHROOMS ARE OUT note below).
3. An acid: wine (white in A per Marcella's canonical; red in B per Nisha) + balsamic finish in B. See WINE note.
4. Soffrito-style FINELY DICED aromatics: yellow onion always in; celery/carrot/garlic vary.
5. Long simmer intent (3+ hours for A; ~55 min for B).
6. Dairy in A (milk); Nisha's B is dairy-free (a commenter noted the sauce could use a dairy component).
7. Served over pasta.

=== WINE — WHITE AND RED BOTH APPEAR ===

Both white and red wine appear frequently across canonical bolognese recipes:
- VARIANT A (Marcella): WHITE wine, canonically. Milk goes in first as a protective coat; white wine follows.
- VARIANT B (Nisha): RED wine, canonically. Deglazes the tomato-paste fond after it caramelizes.
- CROSS-USE: either wine can work in either variant if that's what you have. Marcella's original is white; Nisha's original is red. Sticking to canonical is safer, but the family absorbs either.

Both wines are primary ingredients in this file for that reason.

=== MUSHROOMS ARE OUT — LENTILS + TOASTED WALNUTS ARE THE VEGETARIAN PATH ===

Hardened rule: mushrooms are OUT of bolognese. This file used to include two mushroom-based variants (ATK mushroom bolognese and my own mushroom+lentil mix); both removed.

Reasoning: mushrooms in a bolognese distract with the onion/celery/carrot soffrito base and start to read STEW rather than bolognese. The dish loses its identity. LENTILS + TOASTED WALNUTS (Nisha's approach in variant B) are the vegetarian protein path here — they read as ground-meat-analog cleanly without shifting the register.

IF YOU WANT A MUSHROOM-FORWARD PASTA: see [[pasta-al-funghi]] (lean, dried porcini + fresh mushroom) or [[boscaiola]] (rich, cream + tomato paste + brandy + mushrooms). Those are the mushroom homes in this cookbook's pasta family.

=== DISTINCTION FROM FIRE-ROASTED-MEATBALLS ===

Split off from this file. That dish uses fire-roasted tomatoes (load-bearing) and the meatball shape (load-bearing). Neither belongs in bolognese-shape.

=== DISTINCTION FROM LENTIL-MUSHROOM-STEW ===

That dish is a stew, not a ragu — broth-forward, served as a soup, explicitly anti-canned-tomato and anti-tomato-paste, uses stock not pasta. Don't merge with variant B (which has lentils but different structure).

=== WHY BOLOGNESE GETS THE HEADLINE ===

Variant A is the canonical italian ragu — Marcella Hazan's recipe is the cookbook's reference point. The three non-negotiables (don't brown the beef, milk before wine, three-hour uncovered simmer) define what 'bolognese' means here. Variant B borrows the bolognese shape but doesn't try to be bolognese — it's a distinct vegan dish that respects the shape, not a vegetarianized copy of Marcella.

FAUX MEAT FOR VARIANT A: impossible meat works as a substitute for ground beef. Don't substitute ground vegan meat for ground beef in bolognese — impossible has the right fat profile, ground vegan meat reads off.

NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES IN THIS FILE: regular canned tomatoes only. Fire-roasted is the signature of fire-roasted-meatballs.json.

HERB FINISH — SPARINGLY, BY VARIANT: variant A doesn't take fresh herb finishes well (long simmer + milk-and-nutmeg is its own register). Variant B can take a chopped parsley garnish. Nisha also suggests basil as an alternative garnish — valid (kept secondary) but parsley is the pick.

TAGLIATELLE OVER SPAGHETTI FOR VARIANT A: Marcella was explicit that bolognese is for tagliatelle, not spaghetti. The wide flat noodle holds the meat sauce; spaghetti slides under it. Variant B is more forgiving — long-cut still preferred but ridged tubes (rigatoni, penne rigate) work fine.

GRUYERE OVER PARMESAN FOR GRATING ON TOP — MY PREFERENCE: I prefer grated gruyere over grated parmesan as the finishing cheese. The funkiness agrees with the sauce.

=== VARIANT B NOTES — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE ===

SOURCE: Nisha Vora, Rainbow Plant Life. 10-ingredient vegan lentil bolognese. ~55 min total (much faster than variant A's 3+ hours).

TOMATO PASTE FROM A TUBE, NOT A CAN — LOAD-BEARING: Nisha is explicit and I trust her on this — canned tomato paste leaves a tinny metallic flavor here that ruins the sauce. Tube tomato paste (Amore, Cento, Mutti, San Merican; Whole Foods 365 or Trader Joe's for budget) is cooked at lower temp and preserved with salt (canned is preserved with citric acid) — brighter, truer tomato flavor. This isn't a nitpick; use a tube.

RED LENTILS SOAKED FIRST — 30 MIN MINIMUM: soaking softens the lentils and cuts the cook time significantly. Skip and they'll take 45-60 min to soften in the sauce instead of ~20 min. Red split lentils (masoor dal from indian groceries) cook even faster. Brown or green lentils work as a sub but need an extra 5-10 min and give the sauce more bite (less melt-into-sauce).

WALNUTS TOASTED FIRST — LOAD-BEARING: toast the walnuts in oven or dry skillet BEFORE finely chopping. Toasted walnut is where the meat-analog umami actually lives — raw walnut doesn't deliver the same depth. Same principle as the lentil-wellington walnut-toasting note. Then crush the toasted walnuts in a food processor or spice grinder, or knife-chop very finely. Coarser walnut pieces leave hard bits in the finished sauce.

BALSAMIC FINISH — QUALITY MATTERS OR SKIP: 1 tbsp high-quality aged balsamic. Nisha is explicit that a cheap balsamic just adds watery sourness and doesn't help. Better to omit than to use cheap balsamic. Sugar sub (1-2 tsp brown/coconut/cane) works if the sauce is too sour without.

CRITIQUE FROM A COMMENTER: one reviewer said the sauce reads too acidic without dairy, felt it needed a milk / dairy component. Worth noting if you find the sauce sharp — could try Nisha's balsamic-out / sugar-in path, or add a splash of unsweetened plant milk near the end.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — VARIANTS C + D REMOVED ===

This file used to have four variants:
- Variant C: ATK Mushroom Bolognese (mushroom-only, dairy-forward).
- Variant D: My Vegetarian Mix (mushroom + lentil, marcella-shaped soffrito + milk + balsamic finish + miso).
Both removed per the MUSHROOMS ARE OUT rule above. The mushroom-forward pasta homes are [[pasta-al-funghi]] and [[boscaiola]]; lentils belong here in variant B.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[pasta-al-funghi]] and [[boscaiola]]: the mushroom-forward pasta homes in this cookbook (lean and rich, respectively). Different shape (not bolognese).
- fire-roasted-meatballs.json: fire-roasted tomatoes + meatball shape. Different shape.
- tomato pasta sauce family — [[marcella-tomato-sauce]], [[sicilian-pesto-rosso]], [[vodka-sauce]], [[pasta-piperade]], [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]] (all tagged 'tomato pasta sauce'): the protein-free italian pasta-sauce family. This bolognese file is the protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterpart.
